archived_runs.final_output:
## Meeting Room Booking System v1.0.0 — delivered

All three subtasks are accepted: dev's implementation (subtask-1, reviewed with source-level evidence), QA's independent verification (subtask-2), and the release README (subtask-3).

### What you get (5 files, shared copies in inbox/dev/ plus README.md)
| File | Size | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `booking.py` | 14,708 B | Core logic + JSON store (stdlib only) |
| `server.py` | 9,726 B | `ThreadingHTTPServer` web server + JSON API, serves the page |
| `index.html` | 24,373 B | Single self-contained UI (inline CSS/JS, no CDN, works offline) |
| `selftest.py` | 7,152 B | Plain-assert self-test |
| `README.md` | 3,463 B | User guide / release notes |

### How to use it (2 steps)
1. Put all four code files in **one** folder, then run:
   ```
   python3 server.py
   ```
   (optional: `--port 8080 --data bookings.json --rooms rooms.json`)
2. Open `http://localhost:8080`, or the LAN URL printed at startup (e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:8080`) so colleagues share **one** calendar. Data lives in a single `bookings.json` next to the server — copy that file to back it up.

Day to day: pick a date (defaults to today) and optionally a room → read the per-room 07:00–20:00 timeline to see free gaps at a glance → book room/date/start/end (15-min steps)/title/organizer → a clashing slot is refused with a message naming the clashing booking, while back-to-back meetings are allowed → cancel with confirm + optional reason: the slot frees instantly and the record stays as a greyed-out, struck-through entry behind the "show cancelled" toggle.

### How double bookings are actually prevented
Every create runs inside one `threading.Lock` critical section: read all bookings from disk → validate → scan same-room/same-date **active** bookings for overlap using half-open intervals (`start < other.end and end > other.start`, so 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 coexist) → append → atomic `tempfile` + `os.replace` write. review.reason: Lead reviewed the delivered files directly in inbox/dev/ (booking.py sha c7a208d…, server.py 0c2aecb…, index.html d9f5e7f…, selftest.py 7660e99…) and validate_file reports index.html valid with no errors. Verified in the code: (a) create_booking computes/validates inputs then enters `with self._lock:` and inside that single critical section re-reads all bookings, scans same-room/same-date active bookings with half-open overlap (_overlaps start<other.end and end>other.start), and only then appends and performs the atomic tempfile+os.replace write — so check-and-insert cannot interleave and double bookings are impossible; the conflict error carries existing=other plus a message naming room/date/time/organizer/title for inline UI display. (b) cancel_booking under the same lock flips status to 'cancelled', stamps cancelled_at and cancel_reason, keeps the record (audit trail), and availability() excludes non-active rows so the slot is immediately rebookable. (c) Validation covers unknown room, real calendar date via datetime.date(), 15-min step, start<end, 07:00–20:00 window, max 8h, required title/organizer, with machine codes matching the spec. (d) Dates are compared as wall-clock strings and times as int minutes; no UTC conversion anywhere, so no day shift. (e) server.py uses ThreadingHTTPServer on 0.0.0.0, exposes rooms/bookings/availability GETs and create/cancel POSTs, maps conflict->409 with {error,message,existing}, validation->400, unknown id->404, malformed JSON->400 invalid_json, unknown path->404, and never lets an exception escape the handler; make_server(port=0) exists so QA can test in-process. (f) index.html passes validate_file. dev's reported selftest run shows 28 PASS with the HTTP-layer sandbox limitation disclosed honestly. Accepted as v1; the HTTP-layer socket round-trip is delegated to QA for independent verification.

QA's review is evidence-based and matches what I independently verified by reading the delivered source (booking.py sha c7a208d…, server.py 0c2aecb…, index.html d9f5e7f…) and running validate_file. Confirmed independently: (a) create_booking validates inputs, then inside `with self._lock:` re-reads bookings, checks half-open overlap for same room/date active rows, and only then appends + atomic write — no interleaving window, so double booking is prevented; conflict carries existing=other and a message naming room/date/time/organizer/title. (b) cancel_booking under the lock keeps the record with status='cancelled', cancelled_at and cancel_reason while availability() excludes inactive rows, so the slot frees without losing history. (c) Validation codes/limits and string-date/int-minute comparisons (no UTC conversion) match the spec, so no day shift. (d) server.py maps conflict->409 {error,message,existing}, validation->400, unknown id/path->404, malformed JSON->400, and catches exceptions in the handler. QA's extra value: its own half-open/leap-day/hours/availability/persistence/thread-race (20 threads -> exactly 1 success, 19 conflicts) and in-process handler-dispatch results, which corroborate the design. QA honestly discloses what it could NOT do: dev's selftest.py never reached QA's inbox, socket-level HTTP bind blocked by sandbox, browser JS not executed. Defect D1 (files delivered one directory deep, so `python3 server.py` cannot find index.html in the delivered layout) is a real handoff/packaging problem — I can see it in my own inbox (inbox/dev/inbox/dev/index.html) — and the release package puts all four files flat, which fixes it. D2 (missing index.html returns 500 not 404) is minor and acceptable. No blocker in the source; QA's stated NOT TESTED items are carried forward honestly into my final report.

Release delivered README.md (3275 bytes, sha a4d8ed8a…) into lead's inbox as inbox/release/README.md; I read it in full and it is accurate against the verified source: it names the four files and one-folder layout, gives the exact quick start (`python3 server.py`, open http://localhost:8080 or the printed LAN URL) with optional `--port/--data/--rooms` flags, explains the 07:00-20:00 per-room timeline for availability, booking fields, that conflicting slots are refused with a message naming the clashing booking and back-to-back is allowed, that cancel confirms + optional reason, instantly frees the slot and keeps a greyed/struck-through audit record behind 'show cancelled', states data lives in one bookings.json to back up with one server per file, documents `python3 selftest.py`, and lists honest v1 limitations (no login, no recurrence, no edit-in-place, single server per data file). The submission honestly discloses what was not done (its own file re-copy, validate_file on three files, git init/commit/tag) rather than claiming success — I hold the four validated files flat and have verified index.html with validate_file, and drop the git tag as optional for this delivery.
